resources.string: Pick a PDF to read it. The file is opened from where you chose it; nothing is copied anywhere and nothing is sent over the network.
It needs its open password. %1$d attempts left.
The file could not be read as a document. It may be damaged, or it may not be a PDF.
The file is larger than 64 MB. This version reads the whole file into memory, so it refuses a file that big rather than risking being killed mid-read.
Three wrong passwords. The document stays closed.
The document opened but reports no pages.
The file could not be read from where it is stored.
Changes are made to the copy in memory. Nothing touches your original file until you save, and saving always writes a new file.
The file is written again with AES-256 encryption. The same password both opens the file and permits changing it.
If you lose this password the file cannot be opened. Nothing here can recover it.
A new file is written with no encryption at all. Anyone who gets it can open it.
Saved as %1$s — %2$s, which is not smaller than the original %3$s
Page %1$d removed. Save to keep this.
Page turned. Save to keep this.
This document is not a PDF, so it cannot be changed.
The file could not be written to the place you chose.
The page could not be saved as an image.
This is the only page left, so it cannot be removed.
This page has no text to copy. It may be a scan, and this version does not run OCR.
This document has no password to remove.
The password cannot contain a comma. The engine reads its settings as a comma-separated list, so a comma would cut the password in half and write a file nobody could open.
The password is longer than 32 characters.
A copy for sharing could not be prepared.
No app on this phone can take that.
NextPDF Pro for Android, built on the same MuPDF engine as the Windows build, under the GNU AGPL v3.

Reads and searches PDFs, including password-protected ones. Turns and removes pages, saves a copy, compresses, adds or removes AES-256 password protection, saves a page as an image, copies a page\'s text, shares and prints.
What this version does NOT do

It does not edit the text inside a page, does not add comments or highlights, does not fill forms, does not stamp, does not redact, does not convert to Office formats and does not run OCR. The Windows build does those; this one does not, and nothing here pretends otherwise.\n\nThere is no digital signing, and no visible stamp either — and a visible stamp would not be a digital signature in any case.
